d: Celebrated benchmark worlds in hard science fiction renowned for rigorous scientific worldbuilding and extreme physics.

gaia-1872046609345556480.x: Massive, rapidly spinning oblate planet orbiting 61 Cygni A with surface gravity varying from 3 g at the equator to nearly 700 g at the poles, inhabited by centipede-like Mesklinites.
gaia-1872046609345556480.a: mesklin mesklinite barlennan gravity oblate clement

gaia-4472832130942575872.x: Unique double-lobed planet system (Roche and Eau) sharing a common atmosphere and ocean at Barnard’s Star, explored by the laser-driven Dragonfly probe.

gaia-777254360337133312.x: Lush, Earth-like moon of the gas giant Bear (47 Ursae Majoris b) colonized by political dissidents aboard the starship URSS Alabama.

gaia-3796442680948579328.x: Intended colonial destination planet of the Bussard ramjet starship Leonora Christine orbiting Beta Virginis (Zavijava) before a deceleration malfunction forces a cosmic relativistic voyage.
gaia-3796442680948579328.a: leonora christine bussard ramjet anderson zavijava

hip-71683.x: Inhabited world orbiting Alpha Centauri A discovered through radio music transmissions, leading to the fateful Jesuit first-contact expedition.
hip-71683.a: rakhat sandoz jesuit reshana runa russell

venus.x: Subterranean tunnels and launch stations carved into Venus by the mysterious extinct Heechee civilization, leading to the Heechee asteroid base Gateway.

sol.x: Massive solar energy array within 0.05 AU of Sol, beamed out to power the Theseus mission beyond the Kuiper Belt to investigate the alien entity Rorschach.
sol.a: blindsight watts rorschach theseus scramble icarus

b.s: Foundational astrophysical settings including Mesklin at 61 Cygni (Clement), Rocheworld at Barnard’s Star (Forward), Coyote at 47 Ursae Majoris (Steele), Beta Virginis in Tau Zero (Anderson), Rakhat at Alpha Centauri (Russell), and Gateway at Venus (Pohl).
b.a: Hal Clement, Robert L. Forward, Allen Steele, Poul Anderson
b.r: Mission of Gravity (1954), Rocheworld (1984), Coyote (2002), and Tau Zero (1970)
